sentences.text:
Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 The Honourable Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.21527 Of 2024
Order :

(ORAL) This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to declare the action of respondent No.4 - the Station House Officer, Chikkadpally Police Station, in not registering the First Information Report (for short 'FIR'), pursuant to his complaint dated 19.07.2024, as being illegal and arbitrary.

2. Heard Mr. K. Sai Babu, learned Counsel for the petitioner; and Mr. R. Laxmikanth Reddy, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, and perused the material on record.
3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, having received written instructions, submitted that petitioner is a Xerox shop owner.
One Mr.
Boberoi S.S. Babu - respondent No.5 used to visit his shop and asked him to invest in Diamond business promising 20% returns on investment.

Petitioner has given him Rs.6,00,000/- in 2017, however, respondent No.5 has not given any profits, on petitioner's repeated requests, respondent No.5 issued post dated cheques in August,
2018 for Rs.6,20,000/- which were dishonoured on 12.09.2018.

Pursuant to the complaint of the petitioner, a case in Crime No.389 of 2018 was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 352 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, which was numbered as C.C. No.1216 of 2018 and the same was ended in compromise before Lok Adalat on 28.12.2023.
As per the terms of compromise, respondent No.5 paid Rs.2,00,000/- and for the balance amount he issued a cheque dated 30.04.2024 and the said cheque was also dishonoured.
On 02.02.2024 respondent No.5 paid another sum of Rs.1,00,000/- in cash and did not pay the balance amount.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, further submitted that, as the dispute between the petitioner and respondent No.5 is relating to money and cheque bouncing, the complaint of the petitioner was closed as 'civil in nature' on 07.08.2024.
A notice dated 07.08.2024 was also sent to petitioner intimating closure of his complaint.
5. A copy of written instructions along with notice dated 07.08.2024 intimating the petitioner about the closure of his complaint is served on learned counsel for the petitioner.
6. In view of the aforesaid submissions of the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, no further orders are required to be passed in this writ petition.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.

If the petitioner is aggrieved by the closure report, he is at liberty to invoke appropriate V Merugu Yadagiri vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24527752/
